## What I work on

::: {.card-grid}
::: {}
### Statistical methodology
Survey weighting and raking, calibration, Bayesian inference, and population estimation, formulated as convex optimization where it helps.
:::

::: {}
### Verification for production ML
Preflight checks, distributional drift gates, regression tests for nondeterministic solvers, and reproducible replay. These guardrails make fast iteration, including AI-assisted iteration, safer when correctness is statistical rather than exact.
:::

::: {}
### ML engineering
End-to-end pipelines, orchestration, model versioning, and monitoring on Snowflake, Databricks, and AWS.
:::
:::

## How I work

::: {.card-grid}
::: {}
### Reproduce before you replace
When I migrate a production system, the new pipeline first has to reproduce the old one's published output. Only then do I change the method, and I measure what the change does.
:::

::: {}
### Prove the gap, don't explain it
A reconciliation difference is a bug until shown otherwise. "Solver noise" is a hypothesis to test, not an answer.
:::

::: {}
### Agree on the decision before the code
I put design options and their trade-offs to methodology and engineering partners before implementation, so what ships is what was agreed.
:::

::: {}
### Turn every correction into a rule
I work with AI coding agents under a written playbook. Each rule traces back to the mistake that produced it, and verification is part of every task.
:::
:::

## Background

I have spent more than ten years shipping machine learning in media and advertising measurement, defense, and consulting. Today I own production pipelines that calibrate audience-measurement panels to the population. I hold a Doctor of Computer Science in big data analytics; my doctoral research applied residual neural networks to open-set human activity recognition. Before moving into data science, I worked as a field applications engineer for hardware and research organizations.

See [Experience](experience.qmd) for roles, [Projects](projects.qmd) for things I build on my own time, and [Research](research.qmd) for publications.
